description:
FILED s418.  Surfaced by the #343 ceiling fix: perl-tests/bless.t:179
(`is ref $untied, "main", q(blessing through tied refs) or diag $@`) was a
DROPPED statement since the census began; it now runs and FAILS honestly â
entered docs/fail-baseline.tsv by edit with this task as owner.

    sub TIESCALAR { bless \(my $thing = pop), shift }
    sub FETCH { ${$_[0]} }
    tie $tied, main => $untied = [];
    eval { bless $tied };
    is ref $untied, "main";     # perl: "main"   PCL: "ARRAY"

perl: `bless $tied` FETCHes the tied scalar (get-magic on the operand), so
the blessing lands on $untied (the []).  PCL blesses without invoking FETCH,
so the referent never gets the package.  The general question is WHICH
builtins apply get-magic to their operands â bless here; see the tie roadmap
([[project_tie_status_and_roadmap_decisions]]) before hand-fixing one site
(reference_box_magic_hook is the mechanism).

=== s532d (2026-11-08, Opus): the ROW passes; the diagnosis above was wrong ===
perl-tests/bless.t 105 "blessing through tied refs" PASSES on the s532d tree and left baselines/fail-baseline.tsv by edit (sweep scratch/s532d/out/sweep-own.log in the s532d worktree).  PCL did FETCH the tied operand (twice, perl once); what was missing was #4061 -- a first bless of an ARRAY referent lived on the box only, so `$untied` (the other reference to the same []) answered ARRAY.  The read-count residue is #4325 (filed).  This task holds no row any more; the get-magic question it asks is answered (bless does FETCH) -- close it with #4325 or on its own, the reviewing session's call.
title: bless through a tied scalar does not FETCH â get-magic missing on bless operand
